बॉलीवु़ड से आ गई है एकदम मसालेदार और धमाकेदार खबर! 🔥
रिलीज से पहले श्रद्धा कपूर की आने वाली फिल्म Eetha ने मचा दिया है पूरा तहलका। 🎬
फिल्म के पहले गाने 'Ji Ji Re Ji' पर 517 महिलाओं ने एक मिनट तक एक साथ लावणी के हूक स्टेप्स किए। 💃
यह रिकॉर्ड 24 नवंबर 2025 को पुणे की Zeal University में बनाया गया, जहां अलग-अलग उम्र की महिलाओं ने हिस्सा लिया। 🏆
Asia Book of Records के अधिकारियों की मौजूदगी में श्रद्धा कपूर, डायरेक्टर लक्ष्मण उतेकर और प्रोडक्शन टीम्स Maddock Films व Kathputli Creations को सर्टिफिकेट और गोल्ड मेडल मिले। 🥇
गाने को अजय-अतुल ने कंपोज किया है, श्रेया घोषाल और अजय गोगावले ने गाया है, अमिताभ भट्टाचार्य ने लिखा है और वैभवी मर्चेंट ने कोरियोग्राफ किया है। 🎵
यह गाना प्रसिद्ध लावणी कलाकार विठाबाई के जीवन के उस महत्वपूर्ण एपिसोड को भी दिखाता है जब उन्होंने गर्भावस्था के दौरान मंच पर प्रदर्शन किया था और उन्हें प्रसव पीड़ा हुई थी। 🤰
आपको क्या लगता है, क्या श्रद्धा कपूर की यह फिल्म बॉक्स ऑफिस पर सारे रिकॉर्ड तोड़ देगी? नीचे कमेंट्स में जल्दी बताओ! 👇

ctx.text:
Shraddha Kapoor's upcoming film Eetha has achieved a record ahead of its theatrical release, entering both the India Book of Records and Asia Book of Records. The recognition came after 517 women performed the Lavani hook steps from the film's first song, ‘ Ji Ji Re Ji ’, in synchrony for one minute.
The record-setting event was organised at Zeal University, Pune, on November 24, 2025. Women from different age groups participated in the performance, which was witnessed by officials from the Asia Book of Records. Following the event, certificates and gold medals were presented to Shraddha Kapoor, director Laxman Utekar, and representatives of the film's production teams, Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations.
The achievement marks a promotional milestone for Eetha , which features Shraddha in the lead role and is directed by Laxman Utekar. The film is produced by Dinesh Vijan, Laxman Utekar and Karishma Sharma under the banners of Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations.
The record was set to the hook steps of ‘ Ji Ji Re Ji ’, the film's first song, released on November 17, 2026. Featuring Shraddha performing Lavani, the track is composed by Ajay-Atul and sung by Shreya Ghoshal and Ajay Gogavale. Amitabh Bhattacharya has penned the lyrics, while Vaibhavi Merchant has choreographed the song.
The musical sequence also recreates an important episode from the life of Vithabai, the renowned Lavani performer. It depicts the incident in which she performed on stage during pregnancy and went into labour.
With 517 women coming together for the record attempt, the song has also provided an opportunity to bring Lavani to a larger audience through a collective performance. The recognition in both record books adds another milestone to the film's promotional campaign ahead of its theatrical release.
